details: US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) experienced significant net outflows of $1.79 billion last week, spanning November 16-20. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) was a major contributor, accounting for approximately three-quarters of these exits, including a record daily outflow of about $541 million on Thursday. In contrast, Morgan Stanley's fund saw inflows of 846 BTC. Additionally, spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $314 million in outflows, marking their eighth consecutive week of net withdrawals.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See $1.79B Outflow, BlackRock's IBIT Leads

details: On November 23, 2026, at 02:42 AM (UTC), Ethereum's price dropped below the 1,700 USDT mark, trading at 1,699.459961 USDT. This occurred despite a narrow 1.66% increase over the preceding 24 hours, indicating a recent recovery from an even lower point but an overall sustained dip below a key psychological price level.
title: Ethereum Price Dips Below $1,700 USDT

details: The United Kingdom is set to introduce new regulations prohibiting crypto exchanges from engaging in market-making activities on their own platforms. This regulatory change is part of broader updates to Bitcoin rules and is slated to take effect in October 2027.
title: UK to Ban Crypto Exchanges from Self-Market Making

details: BlackRock's iShares Staked Ethereum Trust ETF could potentially delay redemptions for authorized participants if there's an insufficient supply of unstaked Ethereum. As of Friday's close, the fund held approximately 58,000 unstaked ETH, with redemptions processed in 40,000-share baskets.
title: BlackRock's Staked ETH ETF May Delay Redemptions

details: Bitcoin's price fell below the $60,000 threshold on Friday, November 20, 2026, marking an approximate 8.5% decline for the week and reaching levels not seen since early July. The market is experiencing strong selling pressure, with technical indicators suggesting potential further downside towards the yearly low of $57,800.
title: Bitcoin Price Drops Below $60,000 Amid Selling Pressure

details: A reported US$6.3 billion breach attributed to the Lazarus Group at Binance has raised significant questions regarding liability within the broader fintech sector. This incident underscores ongoing cybersecurity risks in the cryptocurrency space, despite assurances from Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng about fund security.
title: Binance Hack Raises Fintech Sector Liability Concerns
